title: Auto-refresh MADR projections via content-hash manifest, like derived data
context: MADR export could drift silently from the graph. Users had to manually re-export to stay current. The wiki already proved a manifest-based solution works. Touches invariant(s): con_8460b6770f (Config/provider writers must merge idempotently into existing user files and refuse to clobber an unparseable file).
decision: Adopt `.hunch/madr-manifest.json` with dual-hash tracking (graph state vs. user edits) to enable automatic refresh on every capture and detect three categories of drift: stale (graph moved), edited (file hand-modified), orphaned (decision left public graph). Refresh is best-effort and never fails the capture.
consequences: MADR corpus now auto-syncs on capture—users never manually re-export again
Hand-edits detected and preserved; next export won't clobber them
Three drift kinds (not one) map to three distinct human healing paths
Orphaned files detected as potential public artifacts of private decisions (leak detection)
Edge case: prior manifest entries carried through verbatim to avoid laundering preserved edits into the fresh record
alternatives_rejected: Mandatory export on every capture (too much churn if corpus hasn't actually changed)
Single hash instead of two (can't distinguish user edits from graph drift)
One generic drift kind with one healing action (users wouldn't know what to fix)
Validate corpus freshness as a capture gate (wrong failure mode—projection failures shouldn't block graphs)
